findings.governingReading: The eggs and tofu risk being crushed or broken.
findings.explanation: The English incorrectly pluralizes the mass noun “tofu.”

findings.evidenceJa: そんな俺がお気に召したのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether Illya finds him in this flustered state pleasing.
findings.explanation: The English changes Shirou himself as the object of her pleasure into the undefined situation or activity.

findings.evidenceJa: スーパーの買い物袋を手に、イリヤは歌を口ずさんでいる
findings.governingReading: Illya hums or sings while carrying supermarket bags.
findings.explanation: The English omits the bags that complete the ordinary sibling shopping image.

findings.governingReading: The melody carries nostalgia for Shirou.
findings.explanation: The English reduces emotional nostalgia to simple recognition.

findings.highlight: She could only sing by herself
findings.evidenceJa: 歌を口ずさむ事しかなかったのではないかと
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether solitary singing may have been the only thing Illya could do.
findings.explanation: The English promotes Shirou’s sorrowful speculation into asserted childhood fact.

findings.highlight: she had neither friends to talk to
findings.evidenceJa: 帰り道に話すべき相手もなく
findings.governingReading: Illya had no companion to speak with on the way home in Shirou’s imagined account.
findings.explanation: The English narrows absence of a homeward companion into the much broader claim that she had no friends.

findings.evidenceJa: 背の高いカーブミラー
findings.governingReading: Shirou looks up at a tall roadside convex traffic mirror.
findings.explanation: The English identifies the mirror as concave, reversing the optical shape of the object that reveals their reflection.

findings.highlight: a girl, singing with her eyes closed
findings.evidenceJa: 夢でも見ているように、目を閉じて歌っている少女
findings.governingReading: The mirror shows Illya singing with closed eyes as though dreaming.
findings.explanation: The English omits the dreamlike quality of Illya’s reflected expression.

findings.evidenceJa: 弾むように帰路につく少女
findings.governingReading: Shirou imagines Kiritsugu between a young man with bags and a girl proceeding home buoyantly.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes her earlier singing for the buoyant movement specified in the imagined family picture.

findings.highlight: unless she keeps her true self hidden
findings.evidenceJa: ホントウの気持ちを隠さなければ
findings.governingReading: Illya can smile this way only by hiding her true feelings.
findings.explanation: The English changes emotional concealment into concealment of her identity or whole self.

findings.highlight: I just went along with Illya’s lie
findings.evidenceJa: イリヤがそうしてくれたから、俺もその嘘に乗っていられた
findings.governingReading: Because Illya maintained the pretense for him, Shirou was able to continue participating in it.
findings.explanation: The English removes the causal dependence and Illya’s enabling care.

findings.highlight: and going along with our end
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちの終わりに付き合ってくれている
findings.governingReading: Illya has stopped pressing the issue and is accompanying them toward their end.
findings.explanation: The English produces a grammatically broken coordination that obscures her resigned companionship.

findings.highlight: If Illya likes this relationship and wants to keep ignoring that
findings.evidenceJa: イリヤが今の関係を良しとして無視してくれるなら
findings.governingReading: If Illya accepts their present relationship as sufficient and lets the underlying issue go unspoken, Shirou thinks no one need be lost.
findings.explanation: The English turns resigned acceptance into liking the relationship and invents an expressed desire to ignore the issue.

findings.highlight: fate might’ve taken a different turn
findings.evidenceJa: ほんの少しだけ、運命は変わっていたかもしれない
findings.governingReading: Illya says fate might have changed only a tiny amount had he asked earlier.
findings.explanation: The English omits the strict smallness of the counterfactual change.

findings.governingReading: Illya distinguishes Shirou’s technique from ordinary Projection magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English repeatedly calls the technical discipline “magic,” blurring Fate’s central magecraft–Magic distinction.
